rawFindings.title: `GET` as a setting lookup no longer works for sub-apps mounted before `app.init()`
rawFindings.explanation: The new `app[method]` implementation now calls `this.lazyrouter()` before every verb registration. `lazyrouter()` constructs the router using `this.enabled('case sensitive routing')`, which resolves through `this.set('case sensitive routing')`. For a freshly created app that has not had settings inherited yet, `get('foo')` is still handled specially, but `this.lazyrouter()` can now be triggered when registering the first route on a mounted app during boot, before the mount event has copied the p
rawFindings.suggestion: Delay `lazyrouter()` until after the `GET`-with-one-argument settings lookup, and only instantiate the router for actual route registration.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: Create an app, mount it under a parent, and in child initialization call `app.get('view engine')` before any route registration; the call now initializes routing state unnecessarily and can observe uninitialized settings instead of just returning the inherited value.

rawFindings.title: Multiple `GET` handlers on the same path now share no common route, breaking `HEAD` override semantics
rawFindings.explanation: The change replaces the cached base route with a fresh `this._router.route(path)` on every verb registration. That makes repeated registrations like `app.get('/tobi', fn1); app.get('/tobi', fn2);` create separate Route instances instead of adding handlers to the same route. In Express, `HEAD` is dispatched through the matching `GET` route stack; splitting identical paths across distinct routes changes which handler is reached and can skip earlier middleware/overrides that previously applied to t
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore route reuse for identical paths, or otherwise ensure repeated registrations on the same path append to the existing route stack rather than creating a new route each time.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: With `app.get('/tobi', a); app.get('/tobi', b);`, a `HEAD /tobi` request now only traverses the second route's stack; any behavior that depended on the first `GET` handler being part of the same route is lost.
